title: dynamic batching: sequence-length bucketing & padding minimization heuristics (v27)
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: reduce wasted compute from padding in continuous/dynamic batching by grouping requests into sequence-length buckets and tuning padding thresholds. This PR implements a histogram-driven bucketing heuristic, padding-minimization policy, and scheduler hints for kernel selection and KV-cache affinity. The goal is measurable latency tail and throughput improvements for mixed-length workloads without increasing scheduling jitter or violating per-route SLOs.

What changed (high level):
- New bucketing logic that builds and maintains a recent sequence-length histogram per worker pool and derives bucket boundaries using a configurable percentile target (default 90th percentile).
- Padding minimization policy: when forming a batch, prefer smaller buckets to reduce max padding; allow controlled padding up to a max_padding_ratio (default 0.15) to avoid starvation.
- Batch formation now includes a dynamic max_batch_bytes gate (sequence_len * tokens * model_factor) to prevent oversized batches for long-seq heavy models.
- Scheduler hints: we attach bucket_id + expected_max_len to requests so runtime can pick specialized kernels or memory layouts (e.g., fused attention kernels for short sequences).
- KV-cache affinity: when a request is part of an active cached prefix, the scheduler attempts to keep it on the same worker to reuse the KV cache; heuristics fall back after a configurable TTL.
- Metrics and tracing: added per-bucket metrics (count, avg_padding_ratio, avg_latency) and spans for batch-formation path to aid debugging and regression detection.
- Tests: new deterministic simulation test and end-to-end perf bench that exercises mixed-length traffic patterns.

Checklist:
- [x] Implement histogram & bucketing algorithm
- [x] Integrate padding-minimization during batch formation
- [x] Add scheduler hints for kernel selection and KV affinity
- [x] Expose config knobs (percentile_target, max_padding_ratio, min_bucket_size, histogram_window_s)
- [x] Add unit & integration tests
- [x] Run perf benchmarks and iterate

Design notes (short):
- We keep the runtime-side API change minimal: requests carry optional metadata (bucket_hint, expected_max_len, kv_affinity_key). The batcher still enforces SLOs and earliest-deadline-first within buckets.
- Buckets are recomputed periodically from a sliding window histogram to avoid noisy reconfiguration. To prevent fragmentation we enforce a min_bucket_size and merge small neighboring buckets.
- Padding minimization trades off throughput for reduced wasted tokens; to stay within throughput SLOs we allow a global soft_min_batch_fill that triggers cross-bucket merging when aggregate throughput drops below threshold.

Why now: several customer workloads (PLG chat endpoints) showed up to 30% wasted tokens due to naive padding on mixed-length sequences. This approach preserves latency guarantees while reducing unit token cost.

Links: RFC: docs/rfc/dynamic-batching-seqlen.md, benchmark harness: bench/perf/bench_seqlen_bucketing.py, related Linear: ENG-1423, ENG-1589.
change_summary: Adds histogram-driven sequence-length bucketing, padding minimization policy, scheduler hints for kernel selection and KV-cache affinity, metrics, tests and perf bench. Exposes config knobs and ties into existing batch formation path.
commits: feat(batching): add seqlen histogram and bucket generator
feat(batching): padding minimization during batch formation
feat(scheduler): attach bucket_hint + kv_affinity to request metadata
perf: kernel selection hints and minor runtime optimizations
test: deterministic batching simulation and integration test
docs: RFC for seqlen bucketing and runtime notes
chore: perf bench and benchmark harness updates
review_comments: Jonas Reed: Can we make the histogram window configurable per-pool? In high-traffic pools the default 10s window is noisy.
Aisha Patel: Added histogram_window_s config and fallback to a decayed average when traffic is low (see heuristics.rs).
Maya Chen: Found a race in the deterministic simulation that caused flakiness on CI. Suggest seeding RNG and removing time-dependent sleep in test harness.
Aisha Patel: Fixed test harness, forced deterministic seeds and added retries in the sim harness. CI green locally.
Liam O'Connor: Approving after ensuring metrics names match observability conventions and adding an alert for avg_padding_ratio > 0.25 on production pools.
Maya Chen: Noted perf regression on a corner case (long-tail of 4096 tokens). Added a gate to prevent large batches for >2048 sequences and updated bench results.
performance_results: Mixed-length synthetic workload (short: 60%, medium: 30%, long: 10%): output token cost reduced by 18%
Throughput (tokens/s) on p4d: +6% on average after kernel hinting
Worst-case long-seq path: slight tail increase (+3%) if aggressive bucketing is enabled; mitigated by max_batch_bytes gate
Bench harness: bench_seqlen_bucketing.py reproduces distributions and reports per-bucket metrics used in PR
release_notes: Improves dynamic batching efficiency by grouping requests by recent sequence-length distributions and reducing padding overhead. Adds config knobs for percentile target and max padding ratio. Observability added for per-bucket metrics. Non-breaking; default config conservative.
